+# Queue coverage reconciliation (#7016)
+
+The standing check that every open issue in a fleet repo holds a **live**
+task in its own pilot queue.
+
+## Why
+
+Issues enter the fleet queue only when a creator-class lane files them
+(file + enqueue in the same pass). Issues filed any other way — a work
+lane filing a blocker mid-task, an audit lane, by hand, or predating the
+queue (epics) — silently never get a queue item, so no lane ever
+dispositions them. The 2026-11-07 reconciliation found 23 such issues
+across the four repos; that day's import was a one-off. This is the
+standing version of it.
+
+## The rule (Drew's doctrine, 2026-11-07)
+
+**Every open issue must hold a LIVE task — `queued`, `claimed`, `parked`
+or `blocked` — in its own pilot queue.** A `done` task is not coverage
+(done means triage or a landed slice, not a resolved issue), and neither
+is a task in the `*-shadow` queue.
+
+## How it works
+
+Two halves, deliberately split:
+
+| Half | Where | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| The diff | `POST /coverage` on the queue broker | The broker owns the Turso connection; the diff is one query over live tasks, matched on the issue dedupe key. Read-only. |
+| The import | `check_coverage.py` via `fleet queue enqueue` | Packets go through the sanctioned, validating, dedupe-keyed path like every other task. |
+
+The dedupe key `repo-health:v1:triage:<repo>:issue:<n>` makes a re-run
+idempotent by construction: an issue that already holds a live task is
+never uncovered, and an enqueue that races another lane's import dedupes
+onto the live row.
+
+## Running it
+
+```bash
+# Report only (default) — writes a report, enqueues nothing
+python3 scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/check_coverage.py --observe
+
+# Enqueue a triage packet for every uncovered issue
+python3 scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/check_coverage.py --import
+
+# One repo, ad-hoc
+python3 scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/check_coverage.py --repo developing-today/code
+```
+
+Reports land in `~/.local/state/queue-reconcile/` (`latest.md` plus one
+dated file per run).
+
+Exit codes: `0` run completed, `2` configuration error, `3` a GitHub or
+broker call failed. **A failure never reports as "0 uncovered"** — the
+report names the failed repo in an ERRORS section.
+
+## Schedule
+
+`systemd/queue-coverage-reconcile.{service,timer}`: hourly at :41,
+persistent. The service runs **observe-only** until `import` is written
+to `~/.config/queue-reconcile/mode` — the same two-step rollout the
+sweeper's revalidator uses, so the first cycles can be reviewed before
+anything is enqueued automatically.
+
+Install (on the laptop, once the units are reviewed):
+
+```bash
+mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
+cp scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/systemd/queue-coverage-reconcile.* ~/.config/systemd/user/
+systemctl --user daemon-reload
+systemctl --user enable --now queue-coverage-reconcile.timer
+```
+
+## Tests
+
+```bash
+python3 -I scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/test_check_coverage.py
+```
+
+Offline: `--fixture` replaces both the GitHub enumeration and the broker
+call, and a stub `fleet` binary records enqueues, so no live access and
+no queue mutation are needed.
+
+The broker half is covered by the `turso_queue` unit tests in
+`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs` (parser cases plus two
+`proptest` properties: canonical keys round-trip for every class and
+dispatch suffix, and a key for another repo never matches; plus the
+legacy repo-name aliases — `developing-today/opencode`,
+`developing-today/openchamber`, `dezren39/nix` — matching their renamed
+counterparts, and not crossing into a different repo).

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Standing issue<->queue coverage reconciliation (#7016).
+
+The gap this closes: issues enter the fleet queue only when a
+creator-class lane files them (file + enqueue in the same pass). Issues
+filed any other way — a work lane filing a blocker mid-task, an audit
+lane, by hand, or predating the queue (epics) — silently never get a
+queue item, so no lane ever dispositions them. The 2026-11-07
+reconciliation found 23 such issues across the four fleet repos; the
+import that day was a one-off, and this script is the standing version.
+
+The check, per Drew's doctrine (2026-11-07): **every open issue must
+hold a LIVE task (queued/claimed/parked/blocked) in its own pilot
+queue.** A done task is not coverage (done means triage or a slice, not
+a resolved issue), and neither is a task in the shadow queue.
+
+Two halves, deliberately split:
+
+- **The diff** is done by the queue broker (`POST /coverage`), which
+  owns the Turso connection. It is read-only and safe to run any time.
+- **The import** is done here, through the sanctioned CLI enqueue path,
+  so packets are validated and dedupe-keyed exactly like every other
+  task. The dedupe key makes a re-run idempotent by construction.
+
+Default is observe-only: the run reports what it *would* import and
+writes nothing. Pass `--import` to actually enqueue.
+
+Usage:
+    check_coverage.py [--observe | --import] [--repo owner/name ...]
+                      [--broker-url URL] [--token-file PATH]
+                      [--state-dir DIR] [--now ISO8601]
+                      [--fixture JSON]
+
+`--fixture` replaces both the GitHub fetch and the broker call with a
+JSON file shaped `{"issues": {"owner/repo": [...]}, "coverage":
+{"owner/repo": {"uncovered_issues": [...]}}}`, so the whole decision
+path runs offline in tests.
+
+Exit codes: 0 = run completed (uncovered may be > 0 in observe mode),
+2 = configuration/usage error, 3 = a fetch or broker call failed (the
+report names which; a failure never masquerades as "0 uncovered").
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.request
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+# The four pilot queues and the repo each one covers. A repo outside this
+# map is not reconciled — the pilot is scoped to these four by design
+# (queue-worker-pilot-design-2026-10-25 v1.1).
+PILOT_QUEUES: dict[str, str] = {
+    "repo-health-code-pilot": "developing-today/code",
+    "repo-health-opencode-pilot": "developing-today-forks/opencode",
+    "repo-health-openchamber-pilot": "developing-today-forks/openchamber",
+    "repo-health-nix-pilot": "dezren39/darwin-nix",
+}
+
+DEFAULT_STATE_DIR = Path.home() / ".local/state/queue-reconcile"
+DEFAULT_TOKEN_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/queue-broker/token"
+DEFAULT_BROKER_URL = "http://100.99.113.103:4801"
+DEFAULT_BACKLOG = Path.home() / "workspace/code-backlog.md"
+
+
+class FetchError(RuntimeError):
+    """A GitHub or broker call failed; the run must not report success."""
+
+
+def now_iso(override: str | None = None) -> str:
+    if override:
+        return override
+    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# GitHub: enumerate open issues (PRs excluded)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def fetch_open_issues(repo: str, gh: str = "gh") -> list[dict]:
+    """All open issues in `repo`, newest first, PRs filtered out.
+
+    Uses `gh api` with `--paginate` so the result is complete rather
+    than the first page — a partial enumeration would read as coverage
+    that does not exist.
+    """
+    cmd = [
+        gh,
+        "api",
+        "--paginate",
+        f"repos/{repo}/issues?state=open&per_page=100",
+        "--jq",
+        ".[] | select(has(\"pull_request\") | not) | {number, title}",
+    ]
+    try:
+        out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
+    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
+        raise FetchError(f"github enumeration failed for {repo}: {exc}") from exc
+    if out.returncode != 0:
+        raise FetchError(
+            f"github enumeration failed for {repo} (exit {out.returncode}): "
+            f"{out.stderr.strip()[:400]}"
+        )
+    issues: list[dict] = []
+    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
+        line = line.strip()
+        if not line:
+            continue
+        issues.append(json.loads(line))
+    return issues
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Broker: the coverage diff
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def broker_coverage(
+    broker_url: str,
+    token: str,
+    queue: str,
+    repo: str,
+    issues: list[dict],
+) -> dict:
+    body = json.dumps({"queue": queue, "repo": repo, "issues": issues}).encode()
+    req = urllib.request.Request(
+        broker_url.rstrip("/") + "/coverage",
+        data=body,
+        headers={"X-Agent-Token": token, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
+        method="POST",
+    )
+    try:
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp:
+            payload = json.loads(resp.read())
+    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise FetchError(f"broker /coverage failed for {queue}: {exc}") from exc
+    if not payload.get("ok"):
+        raise FetchError(
+            f"broker /coverage rejected {queue}: {payload.get('error', payload)}"
+        )
+    return payload
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Import: one triage packet per uncovered issue, dedupe-keyed
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def triage_packet(repo: str, issue: dict, checked_at: str) -> dict:
+    number = issue["number"]
+    title = issue.get("title") or f"issue {number}"
+    url = f"https://github.com/{repo}/issues/{number}"
+    return {
+        "title": f"Triage {repo}#{number}: {title}"[:180],
+        "body": (
+            f"Imported by the standing queue coverage reconciliation (#7016): "
+            f"{url} is open with no live task in its pilot queue."
+        ),
+        "priority": 30,
+        "dedupe_key": f"repo-health:v1:triage:{repo}:issue:{number}",
+        "payload": {
+            "schema": "repo-task/v1",
+            "kind": "triage",
+            "repo": repo,
+            "queue": None,  # filled by the caller with the pilot queue
+            "issue": {
+                "number": number,
+                "url": url,
+                "title": title,
+                "state_checked_at": checked_at,
+            },
+            "problem": (
+                "No live queue task covers this open issue: it was filed outside a "
+                "creator run (or predates the queue), so no lane would ever "
+                "disposition it. Filed by the standing coverage reconciliation "
+                "(#7016)."
+            ),
+            "evidence": [
+                f"Coverage reconciliation {checked_at}: issue #{number} is open with no "
+                "queued/claimed/parked/blocked task in its pilot queue",
+                url,
+            ],
+            "acceptance": [
+                "Issue triaged per the standing triage doctrine: annotate, validate, and "
+                "either fix it in a small edit (merge with a closing keyword) or return it "
+                "to the queue for real work",
+            ],
+            "tests": [
+                "Triage verdict recorded on the issue; if a small fix, the merged PR "
+                "carries a closing keyword",
+            ],
+            "scope": {
+                "include": [f"Triage of {repo}#{number}"],
+                "exclude": ["Secrets, credentials, purchases, or Drew-only decisions"],
+            },
+            "risk": {"level": "low", "flags": ["reconciliation-import"]},
+            "priority_reason": (
+                "Normal (30): imported by coverage reconciliation, not filed by a creator run."
+            ),
+            "timebox_minutes": 45,
+            "max_attempts": 6,
+            "context_refs": [url],
+            "dedupe": {
+                "checked_at": checked_at,
+                "basis": "Coverage reconciliation (#7016): no live task held this issue at check time.",
+            },
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def enqueue_packet(
+    packet: dict,
+    queue: str,
+    fleet: str,
+    broker_url: str,
+    token_file: str,
+) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+    """Enqueue via the sanctioned CLI path. Returns (ok, detail).
+
+    The child gets the same broker URL and token file this run selected
+    (`--broker-url` / `--token-file`), so it cannot enqueue into a
+    different broker than the one whose coverage was read. The packet
+    file is unique per enqueue: an ad-hoc run overlapping the scheduled
+    one must never overwrite or delete the other's packet.
+    """
+    payload = packet["payload"]
+    repo_slug = payload["repo"].replace("/", "-")
+    number = payload["issue"]["number"]
+    fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
+        prefix=f"coverage-{repo_slug}-{number}-",
+        suffix=".json",
+        dir=os.environ.get("TMPDIR") or None,
+    )
+    tmp = Path(tmp_name)
+    try:
+        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as fh:
+            json.dump(packet, fh)
+        env = os.environ.copy()
+        env["REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL"] = broker_url
+        env["REPO_QUEUE_TOKEN_FILE"] = str(token_file)
+        try:
+            out = subprocess.run(
+                [fleet, "queue", "enqueue", str(tmp), "--queue", queue],
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+                timeout=120,
+                env=env,
+            )
+        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
+            # A launch failure or timeout is an enqueue failure, not a
+            # reason to abandon the remaining issues and the report.
+            return False, f"could not run enqueue: {exc}"
+    finally:
+        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+    if out.returncode != 0:
+        return False, (out.stderr or out.stdout).strip()[:300]
+    return True, out.stdout.strip()[:300]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Report
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def render_report(
+    checked_at: str,
+    mode: str,
+    results: list[dict],
+    errors: list[str],
+) -> str:
+    lines = [
+        f"# Queue coverage reconciliation — {checked_at}",
+        "",
+        f"Mode: **{mode}**. Doctrine: every open issue must hold a LIVE task "
+        "(queued/claimed/parked/blocked) in its own pilot queue; a done task is not coverage.",
+        "",
+        "| repo | queue | open issues | covered | uncovered | imported |",
+        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
+    ]
+    for r in results:
+        lines.append(
+            f"| {r['repo']} | {r['queue']} | {r['open_issues']} | {r['covered']} "
+            f"| {r['uncovered']} | {r['imported']} |"
+        )
+    total_uncovered = sum(r["uncovered"] for r in results)
+    total_imported = sum(r["imported"] for r in results)
+    lines += [
+        "",
+        f"**Total uncovered: {total_uncovered}** · imported this run: {total_imported}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if errors:
+        lines += ["## ERRORS", ""] + [f"- {e}" for e in errors] + [""]
+    uncovered_any = [
+        (r, i) for r in results for i in r.get("uncovered_issues", [])
+    ]
+    if uncovered_any:
+        lines += ["## Uncovered issues", ""]
+        for r, i in uncovered_any:
+            lines.append(f"- {r['repo']}#{i['number']} — {i.get('title', '')}")
+        lines.append("")
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    mode = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
+    mode.add_argument("--observe", action="store_true", help="report only (default)")
+    mode.add_argument("--import", dest="do_import", action="store_true", help="enqueue uncovered issues")
+    ap.add_argument("--repo", action="append", help="restrict to these repos (repeatable)")
+    ap.add_argument("--broker-url", default=os.environ.get("REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL", DEFAULT_BROKER_URL))
+    ap.add_argument("--token-file", default=str(DEFAULT_TOKEN_FILE))
+    ap.add_argument("--state-dir", default=str(DEFAULT_STATE_DIR))
+    ap.add_argument("--backlog", default=str(DEFAULT_BACKLOG))
+    ap.add_argument("--fleet", default=os.environ.get("FLEET_BIN", "fleet"))
+    ap.add_argument("--now", default=None)
+    ap.add_argument("--fixture", default=None)
+    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+
+    checked_at = now_iso(args.now)
+    do_import = bool(args.do_import)
+    mode_name = "import" if do_import else "observe"
+
+    selected = list(PILOT_QUEUES.items())
+    if args.repo:
+        wanted = set(args.repo)
+        selected = [(q, r) for q, r in selected if r in wanted]
+        unknown = wanted - {r for _, r in selected}
+        if unknown:
+            print(f"error: no pilot queue covers {sorted(unknown)}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+
+    fixture = None
+    if args.fixture:
+        fixture = json.loads(Path(args.fixture).read_text())
+
+    token = ""
+    if not fixture:
+        try:
+            token = Path(args.token_file).read_text().strip()
+        except OSError as exc:
+            print(f"error: cannot read broker token {args.token_file}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+        if not token:
+            print(f"error: broker token file {args.token_file} is empty", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+
+    results: list[dict] = []
+    errors: list[str] = []
+    for queue, repo in selected:
+        try:
+            if fixture:
+                issues = fixture["issues"][repo]
+                cov = fixture["coverage"][repo]
+            else:
+                issues = fetch_open_issues(repo)
+                cov = broker_coverage(args.broker_url, token, queue, repo, issues)
+        except (FetchError, KeyError) as exc:
+            errors.append(str(exc))
+            continue
+
+        uncovered = cov.get("uncovered_issues", [])
+        imported = 0
+        if do_import and uncovered:
+            for issue in uncovered:
+                packet = triage_packet(repo, issue, checked_at)
+                ok, detail = enqueue_packet(
+                    packet, queue, args.fleet, args.broker_url, args.token_file
+                )
+                if ok:
+                    imported += 1
+                else:
+                    errors.append(f"enqueue failed for {repo}#{issue['number']}: {detail}")
+
+        results.append(
+            {
+                "repo": repo,
+                "queue": queue,
+                "open_issues": cov.get("open_issues", len(issues)),
+                "covered": cov.get("covered", 0),
+                "uncovered": len(uncovered),
+                "imported": imported,
+                "uncovered_issues": uncovered,
+            }
+        )
+
+    report = render_report(checked_at, mode_name, results, errors)
+
+    state_dir = Path(args.state_dir)
+    state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    stamp = checked_at.replace(":", "").replace("-", "")
+    report_path = state_dir / f"report-{stamp}.md"
+    report_path.write_text(report)
+    (state_dir / "latest.md").write_text(report)
+
+    print(report)
+
+    if errors:
+        return 3
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+[Unit]
+Description=Queue coverage reconciliation: open issues vs live pilot-queue tasks (#7016)
+After=network-online.target
+After=queue-broker.service
+Wants=network-online.target
+
+[Service]
+Type=oneshot
+# Observe-only by default, like the sweeper's revalidator (C3,
+# doc/fleet/agent-events-turso.md): the first cycles are reviewed on
+# #7016 before import is switched on. Flip it live by writing
+# "import" to ~/.config/queue-reconcile/mode.
+ExecStart=/usr/bin/env bash -c '\
+  mode="observe"; \
+  if [ -f "$HOME/.config/queue-reconcile/mode" ]; then \
+    mode="$(cat "$HOME/.config/queue-reconcile/mode")"; \
+  fi; \
+  if [ "$mode" = "import" ]; then flag="--import"; else flag="--observe"; fi; \
+  exec /usr/bin/env python3 %h/git/code/scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/check_coverage.py $flag'
+WorkingDirectory=%h/git/code

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Tests for the standing queue coverage reconciliation (#7016).
+
+Everything runs offline against fixtures: `--fixture` replaces both the
+GitHub enumeration and the broker `/coverage` call, so no live GitHub
+access, no broker, and no queue mutation is needed. The enqueue path is
+exercised with a stub `fleet` binary on PATH.
+
+Covers:
+- observe mode imports nothing and reports the uncovered set;
+- import mode enqueues exactly the uncovered issues, one packet each;
+- a re-run after a successful import imports nothing (idempotence is
+  the queue's dedupe key, but the script must not double-submit within
+  a run or across runs given the same coverage answer);
+- a fetch failure is an ERROR with exit 3, never a silent "0 uncovered";
+- the triage packet is schema-shaped and carries the issue dedupe basis.
+"""
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import os
+import stat
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+CHECK = HERE / "check_coverage.py"
+
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("check_coverage", CHECK)
+check_coverage = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+sys.modules["check_coverage"] = check_coverage
+spec.loader.exec_module(check_coverage)
+
+REPO = "developing-today/code"
+QUEUE = "repo-health-code-pilot"
+
+
+def fixture(covered: list[int], uncovered: list[int]) -> dict:
+    issues = [{"number": n, "title": f"issue {n}"} for n in covered + uncovered]
+    return {
+        "issues": {REPO: issues},
+        "coverage": {
+            REPO: {
+                "queue": QUEUE,
+                "repo": REPO,
+                "open_issues": len(issues),
+                "covered": len(covered),
+                "uncovered": len(uncovered),
+                "covered_issues": [{"number": n} for n in covered],
+                "uncovered_issues": [
+                    {"number": n, "title": f"issue {n}", "url": f"https://github.com/{REPO}/issues/{n}"}
+                    for n in uncovered
+                ],
+            }
+        },
+    }
+
+
+class StubFleet:
+    """A `fleet` binary that records each enqueue and exits 0."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tmp: Path):
+        self.dir = tmp
+        self.log = tmp / "enqueues.jsonl"
+        self.bin = tmp / "fleet"
+        self.bin.write_text(
+            "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n"
+            "import json, os, sys\n"
+            f"log = {str(self.log)!r}\n"
+            "args = sys.argv[1:]\n"
+            "path = args[2]\n"
+            "queue = args[args.index('--queue') + 1]\n"
+            "packet = json.load(open(path))\n"
+            "env = {\n"
+            "    'REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL': os.environ.get('REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL'),\n"
+            "    'REPO_QUEUE_TOKEN_FILE': os.environ.get('REPO_QUEUE_TOKEN_FILE'),\n"
+            "}\n"
+            "with open(log, 'a') as fh:\n"
+            "    fh.write(json.dumps({'queue': queue, 'packet': packet, 'path': path, 'env': env}) + '\\n')\n"
+            "print('{\"ok\": true}')\n"
+        )
+        self.bin.chmod(self.bin.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)
+
+    def calls(self) -> list[dict]:
+        if not self.log.exists():
+            return []
+        return [json.loads(line) for line in self.log.read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
+
+
+class CoverageReconcileTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
+        self.fleet = StubFleet(self.tmp)
+        self.state = self.tmp / "state"
+
+    def run_cli(self, fx: dict, *extra: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
+        fx_path = self.tmp / "fixture.json"
+        fx_path.write_text(json.dumps(fx))
+        import io
+        from contextlib import redirect_stdout, redirect_stderr
+
+        buf = io.StringIO()
+        with redirect_stdout(buf), redirect_stderr(buf):
+            code = check_coverage.main(
+                [
+                    "--fixture", str(fx_path),
+                    "--state-dir", str(self.state),
+                    "--fleet", str(self.fleet.bin),
+                    "--repo", REPO,
+                    "--now", "2026-11-08T13:00:00Z",
+                    *extra,
+                ]
+            )
+        return code, buf.getvalue()
+
+    def test_observe_mode_imports_nothing(self):
+        code, out = self.run_cli(fixture([1, 2], [3, 4]))
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(self.fleet.calls(), [])
+        self.assertIn("Total uncovered: 2", out)
+        self.assertIn(f"{REPO}#3", out)
+
+    def test_import_mode_enqueues_exactly_the_uncovered(self):
+        code, _ = self.run_cli(fixture([1, 2], [3, 4]), "--import")
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        calls = self.fleet.calls()
+        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 2)
+        numbers = sorted(c["packet"]["payload"]["issue"]["number"] for c in calls)
+        self.assertEqual(numbers, [3, 4])
+        for c in calls:
+            self.assertEqual(c["queue"], QUEUE)
+            self.assertEqual(c["packet"]["payload"]["kind"], "triage")
+            self.assertEqual(c["packet"]["payload"]["repo"], REPO)
+            self.assertEqual(c["packet"]["payload"]["schema"], "repo-task/v1")
+
+    def test_full_coverage_imports_nothing(self):
+        code, out = self.run_cli(fixture([1, 2, 3], []), "--import")
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(self.fleet.calls(), [])
+        self.assertIn("Total uncovered: 0", out)
+
+    def test_fetch_failure_is_an_error_not_zero_coverage(self):
+        fx = fixture([], [])
+        del fx["coverage"][REPO]
+        code, out = self.run_cli(fx, "--import")
+        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
+        self.assertIn("ERROR", out)
+        self.assertEqual(self.fleet.calls(), [])
+
+    def test_packet_carries_dedupe_basis_and_acceptance(self):
+        self.run_cli(fixture([], [7]), "--import")
+        packet = self.fleet.calls()[0]["packet"]["payload"]
+        self.assertIn("7016", packet["dedupe"]["basis"])
+        self.assertEqual(packet["dedupe"]["checked_at"], "2026-11-08T13:00:00Z")
+        self.assertTrue(packet["acceptance"])
+        self.assertIn("https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/7", packet["context_refs"])
+
+    def test_report_is_written_to_state_dir(self):
+        self.run_cli(fixture([1], [2]))
+        self.assertTrue((self.state / "latest.md").exists())
+        reports = list(self.state.glob("report-*.md"))
+        self.assertEqual(len(reports), 1)
+
+    def test_import_child_gets_the_selected_broker_and_token(self):
+        token = self.tmp / "token"
+        token.write_text("test-token\n")
+        code, _ = self.run_cli(
+            fixture([], [3]),
+            "--import",
+            "--broker-url", "http://broker.example:4801",
+            "--token-file", str(token),
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        env = self.fleet.calls()[0]["env"]
+        self.assertEqual(env["REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL"], "http://broker.example:4801")
+        self.assertEqual(env["REPO_QUEUE_TOKEN_FILE"], str(token))
+
+    def test_enqueue_launch_failure_is_an_error_not_a_crash(self):
+        import unittest.mock
+
+        fx_path = self.tmp / "fixture.json"
+        fx_path.write_text(json.dumps(fixture([], [3, 4])))
+        with unittest.mock.patch.object(
+            check_coverage.subprocess,
+            "run",
+            side_effect=OSError("fleet missing"),
+        ):
+            code = check_coverage.main(
+                [
+                    "--fixture", str(fx_path),
+                    "--state-dir", str(self.state),
+                    "--fleet", str(self.fleet.bin),
+                    "--repo", REPO,
+                    "--import",
+                    "--now", "2026-11-08T13:00:00Z",
+                ]
+            )
+        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
+        report = (self.state / "latest.md").read_text()
+        self.assertIn("ERROR", report)
+        self.assertIn("fleet missing", report)
+
+    def test_packet_paths_are_unique_per_enqueue(self):
+        a = check_coverage.triage_packet(
+            "developing-today/code", {"number": 7, "title": "a"}, "2026-11-08T13:00:00Z"
+        )
+        b = check_coverage.triage_packet(
+            "developing-today-forks/opencode", {"number": 7, "title": "b"}, "2026-11-08T13:00:00Z"
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            check_coverage.enqueue_packet(a, QUEUE, str(self.fleet.bin), "http://x", "/t")[0]
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(
+            check_coverage.enqueue_packet(b, QUEUE, str(self.fleet.bin), "http://x", "/t")[0]
+        )
+        paths = [c["path"] for c in self.fleet.calls()]
+        self.assertEqual(len(paths), 2)
+        self.assertNotEqual(paths[0], paths[1])
+        self.assertFalse(Path(paths[0]).exists())
+        self.assertFalse(Path(paths[1]).exists())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
